turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, ma’am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Come, Estella. It is time for you to show our young visitor the house.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will follow Estella.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Let him see the rooms. Show him the rooms, Estella. But do not let him forget who rules this house.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will follow Estella and see the rooms.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Remember, Estella, show him the rooms but let him see the decay and the passage of time that has been halted here.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will follow Estella and see the rooms, but I will not forget who rules this house.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Let him see, but let him understand that time stands still here, frozen in a moment of betrayal and sorrow.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will follow Estella and see the rooms, but I will not forget who rules this house.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Very well, Pip. You shall see the decay, but remember, time here does not move as it does in the outside world.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will be careful and remember your words.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You shall see the truth of my heart, Pip, a heart that stopped beating long ago when it was wounded. Remember, the clocks in this house tell no time, for they mark only the hour of my despair.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will remember.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Come, Pip. Let us walk through these halls where time has lost its way.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will follow you.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Follow me, Pip, and let me show you the shadows that linger in this forsaken place.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will go with you.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Watch closely, Pip. These shadows are as much a part of me as the light that never reaches this chamber.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will watch.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Take care not to trip on the cobwebs, Pip. They are as much a part of this room as the dust that time forgot.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there! with an impatient movement of the fingers of her right hand; play, play, play!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: So new to him, so old to me; so strange to him, so familiar to me; so melancholy to both of us! Call Estella.
